records.text: Scottish Rite Freemasonry originated in France after the Knights Templar were dissolved amid accusations of Baal worship.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: But the Scottish Rite Freemasonry actually originated in France, okay? It was after Jacques de Molay, we would say Jack de Molay, was hung or burned at the stake because the French king was looking at what the Knights Templar were doing and the pope had dissolved the Freemason group because they were accused of worshiping Baal. Baal worship,

verification.notes: Official Scottish Rite history traces the recognizable rite to 18th-century France, so the French-origin component is supported. The Knights Templar were dissolved in 1312, centuries earlier, and historical charges concerned heresy and alleged idol worship, not a documented causal origin of Scottish Rite or specifically Baal worship.

sources.title: Scottish Rite: Where did the Scottish Rite originate?
sources.relevance: Dates the recognizable rite's coalescence to 1763 and Stephen Morin of France.

sources.title: Cambridge: The Trial of the Templars — The Charges
sources.relevance: Summarizes the historical charges as denial of Christ, misconduct, and idol worship.
